content:
While Apple's revamped personal assistant is undoubtedly the headlining feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate, this year's update includes many other new features and improvements that have nothing to do with Siri AI. After checking out my picks of the macOS 27 updates I like best, be sure to also watch my video where I demo each one.

App icon redesign

macOS 27 modifies nearly every built-in app icon to some degree, with completely redesigned icons for Siri, Preview, Chess, and a few others. Other app icons, like Finder, Photos, and Reminders, also received noticeable redesigns, trending toward a stronger emphasis on the Liquid Glass design language. In macOS Golden Gate, hardly an app icon escapes modification, though many changes are quite subtle.

If you watch my video below, you'll see a slider comparison showing how each app icon differs between macOS Tahoe and macOS Golden Gate.

Some of the updates, like for the Photos app, I quite like. But others, like Finder, I haven't fully bought into yet. Feel free to share your thoughts on these app icon changes in the comments below.

Video: macOS 27 highlights and changes

Full HDR support

One of the best things about macOS 27 is its extensive support for HDR across the OS's visual experience. Icons, toolbars, and other elements under the Liquid Glass design language all gain support for higher dynamic range—something users on HDR-capable displays will notice immediately.

To see which elements have additional dynamic range, you can use macOS's built-in Digital Color Meter tool to check where shadows or highlights clip when viewing native SDR values. Be sure to watch my video too, where I explore HDR support in various parts of the operating system.

If you're using a Studio Display XDR, you've already seen the difference, but even if you can't afford Apple's most expensive display, you can still enjoy these benefits on third-party HDR-capable displays.

I previously tried out Asus's ProArt QD-OLED 32-inch 4K display in person, and the HDR effect across various parts of the operating system was outstanding for its panel technology. Unlike Apple's own displays which support Extended Dynamic Range, you'll need to go to Settings > Display and toggle on the High Dynamic Range option to enjoy these benefits.

Most recently I've been using Dell's UltraSharp U3226Q QD-OLED display, and I absolutely love it—I'll have a full review video coming soon. On both displays, HDR elements really pop, like the shimmering cursor in the redesigned Spotlight / Siri AI interface.

Design updates

macOS Golden Gate comes with extensive design updates, addressing user complaints about macOS Tahoe. One of my biggest personal gripes was inconsistent corner radii on some windows.

Of course, that wasn't the only issue addressed, but it was the most important one to me. Other fixes include: the floating sidebar returning to an edge-aligned design, a redesigned toolbar with prominent dividers, and improvements to the Liquid Glass effect itself, including a new slider that lets users choose the balance of transparency or tint.

Streamlined menus

Another major user complaint about macOS Tahoe was the accumulation of unnecessary clutter in menus. In macOS Tahoe, almost every menu item was given a corresponding icon symbol, making the entire menu look like a mess.

When every menu item has an icon, you inevitably end up in situations where no appropriate icon exists, while also making the icons that are already there less impactful. I'm glad Apple has finally fixed this issue.

iPhone Mirroring

The iPhone Mirroring feature in macOS 27 sees three major improvements that make it far more useful on Golden Gate.

  • You can now access Control Center through your mirrored iPhone.
  • You can resize the iPhone Mirroring interface so it's closer to the iPad mini's aspect ratio.
  • You can play DRM-protected content from your iPhone on your Mac without getting a black screen.

Needless to say, iPhone Mirroring has become significantly more practical in macOS 27!

9to5Mac's take

While Siri AI has stolen most of the headlines, macOS Golden Gate is about more than just Siri. In this article I've picked out a few of my favorite new features, but there are plenty of other things worth exploring. Watch my full video for an overview of all the new features, and let me know in the comments which one is your favorite.
